title: Hardik-Arshdeep IPL Trade Gets Formal Go-Ahead, Announcement Expected Anytime
excerpt: Cricbuzz reports the swap has been signed and approved by regulators, with both players keeping their existing fees — Pandya at Rs 16.35 crore, Arshdeep at Rs 18 crore.
body:
• The Hardik Pandya-Arshdeep Singh trade has been signed and received formal approval from the regulators, Cricbuzz reports, with an official announcement expected at any time.
  • Neither player's league fee changes: Pandya stays at Rs 16.35 crore and Arshdeep at Rs 18 crore, the price Punjab paid using their Right to Match card at the 2025 mega auction.
  • Pandya moves from Mumbai Indians to Punjab Kings and Arshdeep goes the other way, after a delay while both players signed off on the papers.
  • Arshdeep's father Darshan Singh has also confirmed the trade is complete, telling a YouTube interview the family learned of it as a surprise.

The blockbuster IPL trade sending Hardik Pandya to Punjab Kings and Arshdeep Singh to Mumbai Indians has its formal go-ahead. Cricbuzz reports the deal has been signed, internal BCCI and franchise sources say formal approval from the regulators has come, and an official announcement is expected at any time. The sign-off is believed to have arrived around midday on November 10, with both franchises formally informed.

This is the step that was still missing when we reported the deal nearing completion on November 8: the franchises had exchanged Expressions of Interest and both players had consented in principle, but contracts and regulatory approval remained. Those boxes are now reported ticked.

Fees unchanged for both players

Cricbuzz confirms there is no change in either player's league fee. Pandya's salary remains Rs 16.35 crore, the figure he was on at Mumbai Indians. Arshdeep, bought for Rs 18 crore after Punjab Kings exercised their Right to Match card at the 2025 mega auction, retains the same salary at Mumbai Indians.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=4DjMAlJszbE

"Pandya's salary remains Rs 16.35 crore, the figure he was on at Mumbai Indians."

Why the deal took a week

The trade was first discussed about a week ago and was delayed, Cricbuzz reports, because the players took time to sign off the papers. After further discussions with their franchises, both came on board and the Expressions of Interest were exchanged with the BCCI. Confirmation has also come from the family side: Arshdeep's father Darshan Singh told journalist Vimal Kumar's YouTube channel the family learned of the completed trade as a surprise, Sportskeeda reports.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DZ68bP5Dajf/

What it means for both squads

Pandya ends his second stint as Mumbai Indians captain and, as PTI reported earlier in this trade sequence, is expected to play under Shreyas Iyer at Punjab rather than take the captaincy there. He has been out of action since IPL 2026 with injury and is rehabilitating at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, according to Sportskeeda. Arshdeep gives Mumbai a left-arm new-ball partner for Jasprit Bumrah, the pairing that made this swap attractive to Mumbai in the first place.

What remains is presentation, not process: a joint official announcement from the league and the franchises. Until that lands, the deal rests on Cricbuzz's sourcing and the family's confirmation rather than a BCCI press release, but every reported step in the prescribed trade procedure has now been completed.
